text:
alex: Heads-up — we saw a sudden saturation event in eu-west yesterday where admission dropped from 95% to 40% in ~90s, lots of 429s. Not classic warm-pool cold-starts, looks like simultaneous queueing + network perf blips.
mira: saw the metrics. latency spiked before 429s, but GPU utilization stayed >85% for a while then regional allocator started throttling.
sam: can you paste the admission logs? curious if token-bucket drain happened or we hit the per-customer cap.
alex: logs (trimmed):
```
2025-11-02T16:12:02Z eu-west admission=95% inflight=120 queue=14 gw-latency=120ms
2025-11-02T16:12:34Z eu-west admission=62% inflight=380 queue=210 gw-latency=480ms
2025-11-02T16:13:12Z eu-west admission=41% inflight=610 queue=900 gw-latency=850ms 429s=320
```
jen-oncall: infra-bot flagged cross-region sync retries around the same time — control-plane retries to private deployments. suspecting cascading backpressure.
infra-bot: incident-note: control-plane retry storm detected 2025-11-02T16:12Z -> 16:20Z; affected region: eu-west; mitigation: scaled warm-pool + temporarily loosened per-customer admission floor.
mira: hypothesis: our warm-pool + admission are currently independent heuristics. when network latency increases, autoscaler still brings capacity but admission multiplier is too aggressive negative feedback causing underutilization and big queues.
sam: propose a smoothing controller: proportional rampback that ties admission fraction to a short-window estimate of effective serving capacity (tokens/sec) instead of raw GPU count. this avoids dropping admission too far when VMs are added but network path slow.
alex: sketch of config i tried in staging — fractional admission with hysteresis and a token-credit ledger per-region:
```
admission:
  min_fraction: 0.15
  max_fraction: 1.0
  ramp_window_s: 30
  token_credit_recovery_rate: 50 # credits/sec per GPU-equivalent
  backpressure_threshold_q: 150
  hysteresis: 0.08
```
mira: i like the token-credit idea. also add a short probabilistic admission boost when we detect added warm-pool nodes to avoid the step-drop. something like: when warm-pool delta > 2 nodes in 20s, gradually increase admission by +10% over 60s.
sam: agree. also suggest capacity-weighted admission so tenants with steady low-latency histories get slightly higher admission during recovery (helps PLG traffic).
jen-oncall: ops note: need safe defaults so we don't over-admit and trigger OOM/host saturation. add a hard cap at node-level GPU slots and keep preempt margin.
alex: rolled a canary config to eu-west staging: added token-credit ledger + warm-pool delta smoothing. early results: peak queue depth reduced 35%, 429s halved, tail latency stable.
mira: awesome. let's create a runbook entry for this pattern and add a dashboard for: token-credit balance, warm-pool delta, admission fraction, queue depth, and per-tenant admission breakdown. also add an alert when admission fraction < min_fraction for >2m.
sam: i'll push PR with the config schema and tests (unit + small e2e harness) and link the repo.
alex: link: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/autoscale/pulls/427 — contains test harness and sim driver.
jen-oncall: schedule a 30m retro tomorrow to review failcases: control-plane retry storms, region-wide network partitions, and tenant spike isolation. cc @mira @sam
infra-bot: deploybot: canary applied to eu-west-staging at 2025-11-03T08:12Z :rocket:
mira: :thumbsup: next step: tune token_credit_recovery_rate per machine class and add offline calibration job to derive defaults from historical traces.
sam: noted. i'll include a CLI for ad-hoc sim runs so SRE can replay different spike shapes.
alex: thanks all. big win avoiding hard warm-pool overprovisioning and keeping costs in check while reducing spike 429s.
jen-oncall: great — update the runbook and drop a short summary in #eng-sre so oncall rotation knows what changed. :white_check_mark:
